Two isolated metallic solid spheres of radii \(R\) and \(2 R\) are charged such that both have same charge density \(\sigma\). The spheres are then connected by a thin conducting wire. If the new charge density of the bigger sphere is \(\sigma^{\prime}\). The ratio \(\frac{\sigma^{\prime}}{\sigma}\) is:

 

[JEE Main 2023, 30 Jan (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_1 & =\sigma\left(4 \pi R^2\right) \\
& =4 \pi R^2 \sigma
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q_2 & =\sigma\left(4 \pi\left(2 R^2\right)\right) \\
& =16 \pi R^2 \sigma
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
\frac{Q_1^{\prime}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 R}=\frac{Q_2^{\prime}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0(2 R)} \therefore Q_2^{\prime}=2 Q_1^{\prime}
\]
\[
Q_1^{\prime}+Q_2^{\prime}=Q_1+Q_2
\]
\(\therefore \frac{Q_2^{\prime}}{2}+Q_2^{\prime}=20 \pi R^2 \sigma\)
\[
\frac{3}{2} Q_2^{\prime}=20 \pi R^2 \sigma
\]
\(\therefore \frac{Q_2^{\prime}}{4 \pi(2 R)^2}=\frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{20 \pi R^2 \sigma}{16 \pi R^2}\)
\[
\therefore \frac{\sigma^{\prime}}{\sigma}=\frac{5}{6}
\]

Substitute V and dVdT into the formula for γ:

Let \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\). Then the number of one-one functions \(f: S \rightarrow P(S)\), where \(P(S)\) denote the power set of \(S\), such that \(f(n) \subset f(m)\) where \(n<m\) is

 

[JEE Main 2023, 30 Jan (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The condition

\(f(1)\subset f(2)\subset f(3)\subset f(4)\subset f(5)\subset f(6)\)

means that all five inclusions are strict.

For each element of \(S\), consider the first set in which it appears.

An element may already be present in \(f(1)\), may first appear in any one of the five gaps

\(f(1)\subset f(2),\ f(2)\subset f(3),\ldots,\ f(5)\subset f(6)\),

or may not be present even in \(f(6)\).

Thus, there are five compulsory categories corresponding to the five strict inclusions and two optional categories.

Each of the five compulsory categories must contain at least one element.

Since \(S\) has six elements, there are two possible cases.

One compulsory category contains two elements, while the other four compulsory categories contain one element each.

The number of such arrangements is

\(5\times{}^6C_2\times4!\).

Therefore,

\(5\times15\times24=1800\).

Alternatively, each compulsory category contains one element and the remaining element lies in one of the two optional categories.

The number of such arrangements is

\(2\times6\times5!\).

Therefore,

\(2\times6\times120=1440\).

Hence, the required number of functions is

\(1800+1440=3240\).

Let \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{n^3((2 n) !)+(2 n-1)(n !)}{(n !)((2 n) !)}=a e+\frac{b}{e}+c\), where \(a, b, c\) \(\in Z\) and \(e=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n !}\) Then \(a ^2- b + c\) is equal to ________

 

[JEE Main 2023, 30 Jan (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The given summand is \(\dfrac{n^3(2n)!+(2n-1)n!}{n!(2n)!}\).

Separating the two parts,

we get \(\dfrac{n^3}{n!}+\dfrac{2n-1}{(2n)!}\).

For the first part,

using \(n^3=n(n-1)(n-2)+3n(n-1)+n\).

Therefore, \(\dfrac{n^3}{n!}=\dfrac{1}{(n-3)!}+\dfrac{3}{(n-2)!}+\dfrac{1}{(n-1)!}\) for the values of \(n\) for which the corresponding terms exist.

Hence,

\(\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\dfrac{n^3}{n!}=\displaystyle\sum_{n=3}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{(n-3)!}+3\displaystyle\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{(n-2)!}+\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{(n-1)!}\)

Each shifted factorial series is equal to \(e\).

Therefore, \(\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\dfrac{n^3}{n!}=e+3e+e=5e\)

For the second part,

\(\dfrac{2n-1}{(2n)!}=\dfrac{2n}{(2n)!}-\dfrac{1}{(2n)!}=\dfrac{1}{(2n-1)!}-\dfrac{1}{(2n)!}\)

Thus,

\(\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\dfrac{2n-1}{(2n)!}=\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{(2n-1)!}-\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{(2n)!}\)

Using \(e=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{n!}\)

and \(e^{-1}=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\dfrac{(-1)^n}{n!}\),

the odd factorial sum is \(\dfrac{e-e^{-1}}{2}\).

Similarly, the even factorial sum is \(\dfrac{e+e^{-1}}{2}\).

Therefore, the second part is \(\dfrac{e-e^{-1}}{2}-\dfrac{e+e^{-1}}{2}=-e^{-1}\).

The complete series is \(5e-e^{-1}=5e+\dfrac{-1}{e}+0\).

Hence, \(a=5\), \(b=-1\), and \(c=0\)

Therefore, \(a^2-b+c=25-(-1)+0=26\).
